# Promoted to repo memory: phase-lifecycle

Cite these in .sofar/repo.md by qualified handle — `phase-lifecycle M<n>` —
which is how `sofar doctor` sees that a promoted fact reached repo memory.

- **M1** (2026-08-13T14:25:11.421Z) — A newly built MCP tool is INVISIBLE to this repo's own sessions until it is published and installed. .mcp.json launches `sofar mcp` from PATH, which resolves to ~/.local/lib/node_modules/sofar.sh/dist/cli.js — the installed release, not the working tree. The same rule the hooks follow (security-hardening M2), one surface further. To dogfood a new tool before releasing, spawn the freshly built bundle as its own stdio server: `node packages/engine/dist/cli.js mcp --root <repo>` driven by an @modelcontextprotocol/sdk Client. Pass an explicit `initiative` on each call (that process has no session), and do NOT call sofar_start_session with the live session id — a second session_started in a log that already holds it leaves a permanent "already started — skipped" fold warning.
- **M2** (2026-08-13T14:25:13.796Z) — Do not grep packages/engine/dist/cli.js to check whether a build picked up a change — it is a 545-byte boot shim (the speed fast/full split) that only chooses between ./fast.js and ./full.js. The actual bundles are dist/fast.js (~170 KB, the hot path) and dist/full.js (~1.2 MB, everything else). esbuild also strips comments, so verify with a code or string literal, never with a comment you just wrote.
- **M3** (2026-08-13T15:01:00.654Z) — A cross-record bookkeeping session MUST carry the target record's existing next action forward VERBATIM. sofar_end_session's next_action REPLACES whatever the record had — there is no merge and no append — so a session that writes into another initiative for a mechanical reason (a phase close, a status repair) and then writes back with its own next action has silently destroyed that record's real one. Nothing warns: the write-back succeeds, the digest renders, and the loss is only visible to someone who remembers what used to be there.

The discipline that makes it safe, used across all 16 records of the phase-lifecycle 4.3 repair: read `Next action:` off the target's plan.md BEFORE writing anything, and pass that string back unchanged. Put your own account of the visit in the `summary`, which has no such alias, and put any observation about the next action being stale in the summary too — never in the field itself. Editing another record's next action is a judgement belonging to that record's owner, even when you can see it is out of date.

Two traps ride along with it:
1. A token starting with `--` anywhere in end_session's args makes the write-back fail with a misleading "next_action: must be a non-empty string". cli-ui's next action contains `sofar status --watch`, so preserving it verbatim through the MCP tool is IMPOSSIBLE. The fallback that works and preserves bytes exactly: `sofar event append <slug> --type session_ended --session <id> --source claude-code --actor agent --payload '{"session_id":…,"summary":…,"next_action":…}'` — one JSON string sidesteps the multi-arg handling. Note the explicit <slug>, which is what keeps that CLI write off the branch resolver (record-integrity M1).
2. session_ended is LAST-WINS, so a write-back with a mangled next action is repairable: append another one with the correct text and the projection re-renders. Verified live this session after paraphrasing commit-attribution's publish command instead of preserving it.
